author: timparsons
body:
Description <!-- Describe your changes in detail. -->
-----------------------------------------------------

Observations (phenotypic data) were missing from exports when BreedBase was the backing service. The cause was that the Observations search endpoint wasn't returning any data. BreedBase was interpreting the `trialDbIds` sent in the search POST body as both Trial and Study DbIds. This is likely due to conflicting terminology between BrAPI and BreedBase: https://gist.github.com/mlm483/b5e1590fdedd0c3dcd116bd29ef19423.


## Testing

1. Upload an experiment with Observations (phenotypic data) to a BreedBase-backed program.
2. Download the experiment's Observation dataset.
3. Check that downloaded file has Observations (phenotypic data).

**Alternatively:**
1. Use this query to find valid folder and program DbIds:
```sql
SELECT germplasm_uniquename, trial_id, trial_name, breeding_program_id, breeding_program_name, folder_id, folder_name, observations
FROM materialized_phenotype_jsonb_table
LEFT JOIN (
    select stock.stock_id, array_agg(db.name)::text[] as xref_sources, array_agg(dbxref.accession)::text[] as xref_ids
    from stock
             join stock_dbxref sd on stock.stock_id = sd.stock_id
             join dbxref on sd.dbxref_id = dbxref.dbxref_id
             join db on dbxref.db_id = db.db_id
    group by stock.stock_id
) xref on xref.stock_id = materialized_phenotype_jsonb_table.observationunit_stock_id
;
```

2. POST to the search endpoint with the folder and program DbIds from step 1.
```
curl --location 'http://localhost:7080/brapi/v2/search/observations/?pageSize=1000&page=0' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{ "programDbIds": ["{programDbId}"], "trialDbIds": ["{trialDbId}"], "pageSize": 10000000 }'
```
3. GET the search result endpoint with the `searchResultDbId` returned in step 2.
```
curl --location 'http://localhost:7080/brapi/v2/search/observations/{searchResultDbId}?pageSize=1000&page=0'
```
The benefit of this approach is that you can try adding  `"studyDbIds": ["{studyDbId}"],` to the POST call, to ensure the endpoint works as expected for search by Study as well.

# Description

We're changing the way that product pages score the creep-o-meter. We'll be moving from selecting the highest score rating to taking an average of the scores. Part of this is also making sure that we account for 0 votes in both the final rating (added "No votes" option) and the scoring (preventing division by zero. I also changed the name of the method to reflect these changes.

For bonus points, I also fixed the "X VOTE(S)" below the voting button to properly account for 1 vote.

5. click on Go To website from the state button
6. click on Edit button > again double click on the image -then click on the right side position of re-order

Traceback-
```
KeyError: 'video_url'
  File "odoo/http.py", line 2134, in __call__
    response = request._serve_db()
  File "odoo/http.py", line 1710, in _serve_db
    return service_model.retrying(self._serve_ir_http, self.env)
  File "odoo/service/model.py", line 133, in retrying
    result = func()
  File "odoo/http.py", line 1737, in _serve_ir_http
    response = self.dispatcher.dispatch(rule.endpoint, args)
  File "odoo/http.py", line 1938, in dispatch
    result = self.request.registry['ir.http']._dispatch(endpoint)
  File "addons/website/models/ir_http.py", line 233, in _dispatch
    response = super()._dispatch(endpoint)
  File "odoo/addons/base/models/ir_http.py", line 191, in _dispatch
    result = endpoint(**request.params)
  File "odoo/http.py", line 717, in route_wrapper
    result = endpoint(self, *args, **params_ok)
  File "addons/website_sale/controllers/main.py", line 619, in resequence_product_image
    image_to_resequence[target_field] = previous_data
  File "odoo/models.py", line 6180, in __setitem__
    return self._fields[key].__set__(self, value)
```

After applying our commit, if the customer got a validation error when the customer attempted to swap the video into the product images at the first position. There is a controller named `/shop/product/resequence-image` which
called, when the customer changes the position of the video.

https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/3ce90ddf33f59a80de34cbafd05679d0817d0076/addons/website_sale/controllers/main.py#L582-L587

The `image res_model` will then receive the `product.image` model when a customer moves a video from the third to the second position, and that model locates the field known as `video_url`. However, when a customer moves a video from the second to the first position, `image res_model` will then receive the `product.product`  model, and that model finds the same field but does not have that field in it.

## 🗣 Description ##

<!-- Describe the "what" of your changes in detail. -->

Microsoft noted in a recent [blog post](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2023/07/19/expanding-cloud-logging-to-give-customers-deeper-security-visibility/) that they are expanding auditing. The change is meant to add a notation in related baseline audit policies to inform readers about the upcoming changes and likely update to baseline policies after the changes by Microsoft are complete.

## 💭 Motivation and context ##

<!-- Why is this change required? -->
<!-- What problem does this change solve? How did you solve it? -->
<!-- Mention any related issue(s) here using appropriate keywords such -->
<!-- as "closes" or "resolves" to auto-close them on merge. -->
The additional audit events previously requiring Purview (Premium) will now only require it if Purview is used for 1 year audit retention (since Standard only supports up to 180 days). If Purview is not used retention for 1 year (say another storage medium or service is used), then Premium licensing is not required.

Letting agencies know of these upcoming changes and the impact on baseline implementation is useful for their own planning.

Closes #503 

## 🧪 Testing ##

Testing involved manual review of existing M365 Secure Configuration baseline policy documents to ensure consistency of language related to audit policies and definition of sensitive accounts.

author: sylvanc
body:
This adds code reuse. Code reuse imports fields and functions from parent types when those fields and functions don't conflict with an explicitly specified member. Reusing code doesn't create or imply a subtype relationship.

This also moves to fully qualified type and function names, allowing `use` statements to be discarded early on in the compiler.

author: peastman
body:
Implements #3445.

`ForceField.createSystem()` lets you specify a `residueTemplates` argument to clarify which templates to use in cases where it's ambiguous.  There are other methods that create systems internally for which this argument would also make sense.  This adds it to `addSolvent()`, `addHydrogens()`, `addExtraParticles()`, `addMembrane()`, and `getUnmatchedResidues()`.

As noted in issue #15257, `astropy/modeling/models.py` was the only non-`__init__.py` file which used `*` imports, which as a whole is a bad thing. This ultimately points to instead creating an `astropy.modeling.models` sub-module which contains all the pre-defined `astropy` models. This however, will result in API changes which require deprecations that are out of the scope of this PR.

This PR starts this process by simply moving `astropy/modeling/models.py` to `astropy/modeling/models/__init__.py` and then fixing the imports. Follow on PRs will make the rest of the moves.

This implementation has a different API than the other implementations as Elixir is not object oriented.

Instead, the api has one function `calculate`, which you call with a list of tuples. The tuples have this signature:
`{name, place, elo}`

and returns

`{name, place, new_elo, delta}`

Needed it for my game [Territoriez.io](https://territoriez.io), and contributing back in case it's useful for other people.

I've used the Pyton implementation as a reference.

The big docstring is useful as it also includes doctests which are runnable by Elixir's test framework.

author: markdecrane
body: Fixes [#2680](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-cdk/issues/2680) Introduces a version compatibility matrix in the new VERSION_COMPATIBILITY.md file Value add here is to better surface underlying provider version information, as well as to have a central location/record to point to when users are trying to find the corresponding terraform provider version to their pre-built provider version. Which can be important for debugging and for knowing which resources are available. **_NOTE_**: There are some outstanding issues with this approach ## Issue with Current Approach I had initially thought that the `package.json` would track the version of the package correctly, and my implementation relied on that. Though what is actually the case is that the version in `package.json` is always `0.0.0`, and the way the project was locally building misled me. You can take a look at what I'm talking about in the section "Updating Versions File on Provider Upgrade" below. I've now found out that the version of the prebuilt provider is only known (and subsequently bumped) in the release workflow, specifically through the script `should-release.js` #### `should-release.js` ```javascript const prefixFilter = `v*`; const listGitTags = [ "git", '-c "versionsort.suffix=-"', // makes sure pre-release versions are listed after the primary version "tag", '--sort="-version:refname"', // sort as versions and not lexicographically "--list", `"${prefixFilter}"`, ].join(" "); const stdout = execSync(listGitTags).toString(); const tags = stdout.split("\n"); if (tags.length > 0 && tags[0].trim() !== "") { const latestTag = tags[0]; console.log(`Found latest tag ${latestTag}`); <---- !WHERE VERSION IS FOUND! ``` #### Next Steps It seems feasible to add to the `release` workflow a step where we create and auto merge a PR with the changes to the `VERSION_COMPATIBILITY.md` file, since we would then know the bumped version of the prebuilt-provider. But, considering the time it takes to iterate on this code region and tempermentalness of this pipeline– I wanted to get some opinions on whether this makes sense to continue work on. I currently have another PR up ([you can take a look here ](https://github.com/cdktf/cdktf-provider-project/pull/342)- maybe give it a review even 😉) that in part solves [#2680](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-cdk/issues/2680) and I am starting to think that the pragmatic approach is to stick to its more simple (yet limited) approach of surfacing underlying provider information. ___________________________________________________________________________ ### Additions to the Codebase A new script has been added, update-version-file.ts. It procedurally adds new version information upon the building of the provider. More specifically this occurs in `build.yml` workflow. In the case where these updates to the provider project are initially being introduced to pre-built provider repos, the VERSION_COMPATIBILITY.md file is created alongside it's first entry. In the case of a provider upgrade, the VERSION_COMPATIBILITY.md file is updated in the build step of the PR it creates. ### Validation of Feature Functionality Since this can't be tested directly (changes involve workflows), I've created two forks for testing purposes. One for the provider project (in order to make the needed changes to publish a separate npm package), and another for a prebuilt provider (that consumes said npm package) to test against. #### Initial Introduction Of Changes As seen in [this commit](https://github.com/Maed223/cdktf-provider-null-test/pull/4/commits/6445d98f39fbbaa0b3e1d010c9d88b387e8a8e34), and on [this PR](https://github.com/Maed223/cdktf-provider-null-test/pull/4) from `team-tf-cdk` for self mutation coming from the changes introduced in `provider-project` #### Updating Versions File on Provider Upgrade [After forcing the provider to track a lower major version](https://github.com/Maed223/cdktf-provider-null-test/pull/9). I then triggered the `provider-upgrade` workflow. The VERSION_COMPATIBILITY.md file on [this PR](https://github.com/Maed223/cdktf-provider-null-test/pull/10) and from [this commit](https://github.com/Maed223/cdktf-provider-null-test/pull/10/commits/e3dd77ddcec1c4cd1d79c0b605c11972d5ecf633) is as follows Note that the middle entry was generated by the `build` workflow in [forcing the provider tracked to downgrade](https://github.com/Maed223/cdktf-provider-null-test/commit/e975218b6bcf4ac8ffd388d41d839e169e7abf11#diff-9134d73e74595ef548197763b257e5d9cff62656660e439b6526ca5fc23a8d48R1:~:text=%7C%208.0.1%20%7C%202.0.0%20%7C%20%5E0.18.0%20%7C) and otherwise wouldn't be present.

# Future changes

- Eventually, make our own post-processor to output properties dependent of multiple physics (multiple dof handlers).

author: soniaconnolly
body:
## 🎫 Ticket

[LG-10886](https://cm-jira.usa.gov/browse/LG-10886)

## 🛠 Summary of changes

This implements the first half of moving ssn to idv_session. Part 2 will remove references to ssn as an attribute of flow_session[:pii_from_doc] and flow_session[:pii_from_user].

When a user moves through IdV, their SSN is currently stored as an attribute of :pii_from_doc or :pii_from_user. As part of moving :pii_from_doc out of flow_session, this gives ssn its own entry in idv_session. 

Reasons: 
- SSN is not actually read from a document; the user types it in directly, so it does not really belong in :pii_from_doc
- It is awkward to handle :ssn during the transition when :pii_from_doc is in the flow_session and also idv_session
- SSN is entered in a separate page for In Person flow and is currently stored separately in :pii_from_user. If ssn has its own attribute, both flows could save it to idv_session, and it becomes more possible to merge these two screens.

 
## 📜 Testing Plan

- [ ] Create account, start IdV
- [ ] Edit SSN in VerifyInfo step
- [ ] Expect SSN to be saved correctly in verified profile
- [ ] Create new account, start IdV
- [ ] Upload error yaml to enter In Person flow
- [ ] Edit SSN in VerifyInfo step
- [ ] Expect SSN to be saved correctly when barcode is generated.

body:
[AJ-1308](https://broadworkbench.atlassian.net/browse/AJ-1308)
Protected snapshots-by-reference should not be allowed in unprotected workspaces.  Future work should rely on terra policy service to identify protected snapshots and workspaces, but to fill in the compliance gap in the short term, this PR checks the protected status of a snapshot by `isSecureMonitoringEnabled` on its root dataset and of the workspace by the `fc-secure` prefix of its bucket.  
In order to check the root dataset of a snapshot, I needed to fetch the snapshot from TDR; this means adding a `DataRepoDAO` to the `SnapshotService`, with associated changes wherever `SnapshotService` is used.

author: pengwei715
body:
Hi @guy1992l , 

This PR is about using the result from the speaker diarization to do transcription. 

1. In the transcribe function, we have a optional argument called `url_path`. This is the path of the result from `speaker_diarization`.  It has the following columns:
- audio_file. # where is the original audio file
- diarization_results  # folder that have the results from Nemo pipeline
- converted_audio_file # path of the converted wav file
- speaker_segments # path of the csv file that have the speaker segments information(speaker, start_time, end_time)
2. In the `_split_audio function`, it split the wav file into pieces based on the speaker segments.
3. In the `_single_transcribe` function, if the segments is passed in, then we loop through each segment to do transcription. In the `whiper` call, we give all the previous conversation as the `initial_prompt`. Concatenate the  result together to get the final result.

### Description
This PR introduces new sorting capabilities to enhance media list management. Users can now sort media lists by multiple fields including title, size, release year, runtime, added date, rating, seasons, and episodes. Both ascending and descending sort orders are supported for these fields.

### Key Features
Adds advanced sorting options to media lists
Supports both ascending and descending sort orders
Allows sorting by title, size, release year, runtime, added date, rating, seasons, and episodes
Adds extensive test coverage for the new sorting functionality
Updates documentation to include new sorting options in library configuration
This feature aims to provide users with more flexible and intuitive ways to manage their media lists, making it easier to organize and find media based on various criteria.

### Documentation Changes:
The sorting options are also reflected in the library configuration section of the documentation, including examples of how to set them.

Addresses the requirements of #24

The new 4.2.0 release of the _aio-cli-lib-console_ library, includes a new function that takes care of the conditional logic to retrieve a workspace credential depending on the type of auth providers. author: ahmad-s792
body:
Improve the reliability and accuracy of SVG getTotalLength
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=258776
rdar://problem/111962327

Reviewed by NOBODY (OOPS!).

Merge: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/blink/+/4767de54b0b1487746440fc3a44ff47e4f8bb671

This PR effectively reverts r190544 and opts for Blink's patch to enable same fix.
The existing code for SVG path.getTotalLength had two problems when
subdividing curves to estimate length. The subdivision terminated when
the straight-line vs curved length was within a fixed limit, regardless
of the scale of the curve. The termination condition for infinite loops
also failed to stop on infinite loops.

This patch fixes both issues. The subdivision threshold now accounts for
the magnitude of the values, so that we give more resolution on very small
curves and less on very large curves. This is consistent with the actual
precision we have in floating point numbers. The infinite loop termination
tracks and examines the total number of subdivisions thus far, terminating
after 20 (which is more than enough - most curves do no more than 10
subdivisions).

We also remove two unused variables and a FIXME that makes little
sense and that we won't ever fix.

author: kalashnikovisme
body:
## What's changed basically?

Presenting **useful and convenient** form objects for Rails applications.

*app/forms/user_form.rb
```ruby
class UserForm < Tramway::BaseForm
  properties :email, :password

  def password=(value)
    object.password = value if value.present?
  end
end
```

## What's changed for tramway drivers?

### Before

*app/controllers/users_controller.rb*
```ruby
class UsersController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @user = User.new

    if @user.save user_params
      render :show
    else
      render :new
    end
  end

  def update
    @user = User.find params[:id]

    if @user.save user_params
      render :show
    else
      render :edit
    end
  end
  
  private

  def user_params
    params[:user].permit!
  end
end
```

### After

*app/controllers/users_controller.rb*
```ruby
class UsersController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @user = tramway_form User.new

    if @user.submit params[:user]
      render :show
    else
      render :new
    end
  end

  def update
    @user = tramway_form User.find params[:id]

    if @user.submit params[:user]
      render :show
    else
      render :edit
    end
  end
end
```

Find more info [here](https://github.com/Purple-Magic/tramway/tree/issue_31#tramway-form)

author: yasoomn
body:
This is a script for controlling the BioShaker atomation module. The shaker is designed to be controlled directly from a robot, however we are using it as a regular plate shaker and controlling it manually. This script facilitates controlling it directly from a computer for day-to-day usage.

    Usage: ./shaker.r [options]

    Options:
            -v, --verbose
                    Print extra output [default]

            -s SHAKE, --shake=SHAKE
                    Start shaking at X rpm. Use X = 0 to stop shaking.

            -o, --open
                    Open the thing

            -c, --close
                    Close the thing

            -t TEMPERATURE, --temperature=TEMPERATURE
                    Heat the plate to the temperature X. Set to 0 to turn off the temperature control

            -p PORT, --port=PORT

            -h, --help
                    Show this help message and exit

author: rmccorm4
body:
Fixes L0_simple_lib--base, and allows requests to be re-used for multiple inferences. 

Adds a sanity check that pending count isn't incremented multiple times without getting decremented in some edge case where a request is PENDING, fails to get to the PENDING state, and ends up in PENDING state again (re-used).

General logic:
1. When a request is created, it is in INITIALIZED state
2. When a request is run, it is set to PENDING state
3. If a request makes it to the backend, it should be in EXECUTING state
    - At this point, the backend takes ownership of the request, and is responsible to call RequestRelease() on it, moving request into RELEASED state
4. If any error occurs before getting to backend, it should hit InferenceRequest::RespondIfError and be set to RELEASED state.
5. If somehow a request didn't make it to backend (EXECUTING state), but also didn't get RELEASED, then it should still be in PENDING state. If the request is to be re-used for another inference, it should call PrepareForInference() which should set state back to INITIALIZED at the start of the cycle. 

If a request were to be transitioned from RELEASED to PENDING/EXECUTING directly, this should indicate a logical error as the request should only execute via InferAsync entrypoint, which calls PrepareForInference ([re]sets to INITIALIZED state) then InferenceRequest::Run (sets to PENDING state).
